key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon-negative scavenger can substantially boost solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: This design suggests a practical route to improve photocatalytic CO2 conversion by co-optimizing catalyst composition for adsorption, charge separation, and transport while using a renewable biological co-reactant.
method: Used layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy to tune surface basicity, polarization, and charge transport.
Compared CO2 conversion with no sacrificial agent, with microplastics, and with microalgae under photocatalytic conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO production about 10-fold and CH4 production about 4-fold relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The reported gains are based on abstract-level comparison, so long-term stability, biomass handling, and scale-up practicality still need verification.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
